reviews.text: As its the first day at Edinburgh, we visited the Maki and Ramen, the warmth of the welcome, the attentiveness of the staff, and the overall atmosphere was excellent. We had the rich, deeply flavorful Garlic Tonkotsu ramen, alongside a side prawn and Squid showcased great ingredients and meticulous presentation. Every dish arrived at the table hot, perfectly timed, and crafted with obvious care. Miss Nabina  was exceptionally knowledgeable, patient, and accommodating, ensuring that every detail of our order was served perfectly. Highly recommended for anyone seeking both incredible Japanese cuisine and a welcoming atmosphere.

reviews.author: Genoa Gray
reviews.text: I have been coming to maki and Ramen renfield for years now. Every time I come here the food is always quick and beautifully presented! The variety of drinks between the cocktails, mocktais wines, bubble tea, and soft drinks means there's something for everyone. Throughout my many times visiting the store the staff has always been extremely helpful and welcoming. I especially love the safe space made for different cultures as well as the LGBT+ community. Even on the days where the staff are clearly busier than was expected, it's clear the staff work very hard to provide the best experience they can every time. I am excited to show my friends visiting from abroad one of my favourite restaurants, for the food and the atmosphere. Keep up the good work maki!

reviews.author: Ruth Flynn
reviews.text: Although the ramen and food were lovely, the customer service was disappointing, especially from the manager. I’ve visited several times with colleagues and friends, hoping each visit would be better, but unfortunately we have left disappointed every time. The staff were not accommodating to customers’ needs, and the overall service lacked warmth and professionalism. What made the experience even more frustrating was that a service charge was already included in the bill, even though it is optional. This puts customers in an awkward position and makes the dining experience uncomfortable. A service charge should reflect good service, not be assumed. The food is genuinely good, but the consistently poor customer service means I cannot recommend this place until it improves.

reviews.author: Afterlife Addict
reviews.text: I gave Maki & Ramen a second chance, and I instantly regretted it. The food wasn’t even the biggest issue. The customer service, especially from the manager, completely ruined the experience. Instead of listening to our concerns or trying to find a solution, the manager was defensive throughout the conversation. We weren’t expecting anything unreasonable, just some understanding and a willingness to resolve the situation. To make matters worse, we were still charged a mandatory service charge, despite receiving service that was far below expectations. It’s disappointing to be expected to pay extra for an experience that left us feeling ignored. What made this even more frustrating was that we had guests visiting from overseas, and this ended up ruining what should have been an enjoyable evening. Unfortunately, after giving this restaurant another chance, I won’t be returning. If you’re looking for ramen in Glasgow, I’d recommend trying Ramen Dayo instead. The difference in customer service and overall experience is night and day.

The trick worked, even with my dexterity problems.  Another female staff member who served us was so amazing and the fact ahe asked twice if there were any food allergies at our table, made me feel the restaurant actually cares. Will definitely be back not only for the delicious food, but the beyond amazing customer service these staff members exhibited.   That goes a long way.

reviews.text: We got in and stood at the door for ages as the service was extremely slow. Even after we sat down, no one came to take our order and we were constantly being ignored. Eventually, a lady came over and took our order. We had to ask her to wipe the table, which she did reluctantly, and she still missed several spots. This left me concerned about hygiene. About 20 minutes after ordering, a different guy came over and told us the ramen bowl wasn't available, which was the main reason we came. We ended up having two starters and then left. I'm really dissatisfied. I must say we were given a £20 gift card to come back, and if it had just been about the food, I guess that would have been fine. But the customer service felt discriminatory and was a big let-down. I can't be bought I would rather be treated with respect.

There seemed to be only one staff member serving the floor, but he was incredibly hardworking and took our order within a few minutes despite constantly being on the move. The food took a little while to arrive, but it was absolutely worth the wait. Everything was fresh, full of flavour, and tasted amazing. We had a great time overall and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommended!

reviews.text: This is one of the worst foods I had in London. reviews.author: Daniel Redknap-Neely
reviews.text: My wife and I visited your location at West Quay tonight for her birthday. Overall we had a good night and enjoyed the food. But there were a couple small things I wanted to mention. On the website it says the restaurant is open until 10pm Monday to Sunday. But we arrived just before 7:30 and were told the kitchen was closing in three minutes and we had to make an order before sitting down if we wanted to eat. This would be fine if it was mentioned on the website as we had driven 40mins to get there and almost missed out. Secondly, we were offered free mochi or a glass of Prosecco for my wife’s birthday (and maybe partially to apologise for the rushed ordering process) but when we got home and checked the bill (the restaurant was closing at 8pm as we left so we didn’t get to check properly there) that were were in fact charged for the (free) mochi.
